conservation.condition_narrative: The support sheet and all media are stable and secure. There are occasional, isolated paper and mat board fibers and accretions on the design surface. There is a repaired tear on the viewer's left edge, outside the margin of media application, near the midpoint of the sheet. This repair remains stable. There is a small pin or tack hole at the center of the top edge of the design area, in red paint, with a slight crease. This hole is stable. There are two small pinpoint losses of black media near the bodice area of the figure. The surrounding media are secure and stable. There are isolated media inclusions and a single accretion. All remain stable and secure.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is a cartridge pad paper used extensively by O'Keeffe for her watercolors starting in 1916 and ending in 1918. The sheet is catalogued in the Georgia O’Keeffe Catalogue Raisonné Paper Survey as moderately thick, cream colored, smooth cartridge paper with a slightly fuzzy feel. It may contain some esparto fiber. 
 
 
 
**Ground or Support Preparation:** None. 
 
 
 
**Design Layers:** Graphite underdrawing is generally visible at the margins of adjacent forms. The work is characterized by dense applications of color in the figure, light applications of color in the backgrounds, with generally distinct and hard edges, generally following the contours of the underdrawing. A technique may have been followed in which single colors were applied to areas of the composition first defined with applied water, with the color allowed to bleed to the established hard edge of the form and then allowed to dry before adjacent areas were likewise wet and colored. Paints appear to be tube-based watercolors. 
 
 
 
**Surface Coating:** None. 
 
 
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** The work is matted using all cotton, acid-free, buffered backing and window mats and a micro-chamber corrugated board backing, enclosed in a Marvelseal envelope and acrylic J-Lar 410 tape sealed to the glazing, framed in a new, standard Georgia O'Keeffe Museum, micro-environmentally buffered and gasketed, white-wash maple frame. The glazing is Optium® tin salt-coated, UV-absorbing, static-free, non-reflective acrylic.
